summary:
Najm al-Dīn Umāra al-Ḥakamī al-Yamanī was a Sunni historian, jurist and poet of Yemen of great repute who was closely associated with the late Fatimid Caliphate of Egypt. Umara ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Yamani was executed by order of Saladin at Cairo on April 6, 1174 for his part in a conspiracy to restore Fatimid rule. His Tarikh al-Yaman is the earliest, and in respects the most important, history of Yemen from the Islamic era.

Umara's legacy extends beyond his own writings, as he played a significant role in shaping the historical narrative of Yemen. His work has been widely studied and translated, making him one of the most important historians of his era. Umara's Tarikh al-Yaman remains an essential source for understanding the history of Yemen during the Islamic period.

His execution by Saladin has become a notorious episode in the history of the Fatimid Caliphate. Umara's story serves as a reminder of the complexities and challenges faced by historians and chroniclers during this period.

In conclusion, Najm al-Dīn Umāra al-Ḥakamī al-Yamanī was a remarkable individual whose contributions to the field of history have endured for centuries.
